mainTopic: Tithing produce acquired from a גוי, the dispute about produce deposited with a גוי, and when the כהן acquires the redemption lamb of a פטר חמור.
overview: This amud opens at the end of רבי שמואל's ruling in the name of רבי חנינא. It says that someone who buys smoothed grain from a גוי must separate מעשר but may keep the portions. The גמרא explains the case: a Jew smoothed the grain while the גוי still owned it. He must tithe because a גוי's ownership cannot cancel the holiness of ארץ ישראל. He keeps the portions because he stands in the place of the גוי, whom no כהן can sue. Next, a משנה from דמאי teaches that produce left with a גוי is treated as the גוי's produce, while רבי שמעון calls it דמאי. רבי אלעזר explains that both sides agree the owner must separate, and they argue only about giving the portions to a כהן. אביי asks how this fits רבי חנינא's ruling. רב דימי answers that one ruling is about תרומה גדולה and the other about תרומת מעשר, and אביי recalls a פסוק that backs this up. Finally, the גמרא returns to our משנה. It teaches that the lamb used to redeem a פטר חמור belongs to the כהן from the moment it is separated.

steps.title: Buying grain already smoothed by a gentile's side
steps.stepSummary: The end of a ruling of רבי שמואל in the name of רבי חנינא: grain bought from a גוי already smoothed into piles must be tithed, but the tithes belong to the buyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: [One who buys grain that is already] smoothed into piles from a גוי must separate the tithes, but they remain his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רבי שמואל's ruling, in the name of רבי חנינא, about a Jew who buys grain from a גוי after the grain was already smoothed into piles. This ruling is the base text the next steps will analyze.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Smoothing the pile (מירוח) is the final processing step that makes grain obligated in תרומה and מעשר. רבי חנינא gives a split ruling. The buyer must separate the portions, but he does not have to hand them to a כהן or a לוי. The next steps explain both halves of that ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Smoothed into piles; the last processing step that makes grain obligated in tithes
He separates the tithes from them
And they (the separated portions) are his to keep

steps.confusionAlert: 'They are his' does not mean he can skip separating. He must still separate the portions; he simply does not have to give them away to a כהן or לוי.

phrases.english: [Grain that is] smoothed into piles, [bought] from a gentile,
he tithes them, but they are his.
phrases.notes: 'They are his' means the separated portions: he keeps them and doesn't hand them to a כהן or לוי.

steps.triggerLanguage: ממורחין מן הגוי, מעשרן והן שלו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ruling of רבי שמואל in the name of רבי חנינא begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grain bought from a גוי after smoothing must be tithed, but the buyer keeps the separated portions.

steps.title: Who did the smoothing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who smoothed the piles: the גוי or a Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about רבי חנינא's ruling: who smoothed these piles? This question sets up the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer matters because the obligation to tithe starts at the moment of smoothing. Whose grain it was, and who did the work at that moment, decides whether any obligation started at all.

phrases.english: Who smoothed them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact case behind רבי חנינא's ruling in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the גוי or a Jew performed the smoothing.

steps.title: It cannot be the gentile who smoothed it
steps.stepSummary: If the גוי had smoothed the grain, no obligation would apply, because the תורה says 'דגנך', your grain, and not the grain of a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the גוי smoothed them, that cannot be: the Merciful One said 'your grain', not the grain of a גוי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first possibility, that the גוי did the smoothing, and rejects it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'דגנך' teaches that only grain finished in a Jew's hands becomes obligated in תרומה and מעשר. If the גוי finished it, the grain would be completely exempt. Then רבי חנינא's ruling 'מעשרן' would make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a possibility the גמרא is about to test)
'Your grain'; the פסוק about תרומה and מעשר
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

phrases.english: If we say that a gentile smoothed them —
the Merciful One said "your grain,"
phrases.notes: This is from the פסוקים about giving תרומה and מעשר, which speak of 'your grain'.

phrases.english: and not the grain of a gentile!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first answer to the question in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that the גוי did the smoothing.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Grain finished by a גוי is exempt because of 'דגנך', so the ruling 'מעשרן' would not fit.

steps.title: A Jew smoothed it while it still belonged to the gentile
steps.stepSummary: The case is a Jew who smoothed the grain while it was still owned by the גוי, and then bought it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, a Jew smoothed them while they were still in the גוי's ownership.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its answer: a Jew did the smoothing while the grain still belonged to the גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up a mixed case. The smoothing was done by a Jew, but at that moment the grain belonged to a גוי. That mix explains why the ruling is split in two halves.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces the correct reading after a rejected one)

phrases.english: Rather, a Jew smoothed them
while in the possession of the gentile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct answer to the question in step 2, after step 3 rejected the first option.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A Jew smoothed the grain while the גוי still owned it.

steps.title: Why he must tithe, and why he may keep the tithes
steps.stepSummary: He must tithe because a גוי's ownership in ארץ ישראל cannot cancel מעשר. He keeps the portions because he steps into the shoes of the גוי, whom nobody can sue.
steps.simpleTranslation: He tithes them, because a גוי has no ownership power in ארץ ישראל to remove it from מעשר. And they are his, because he can say to the כהן: 'I come on the strength of a man you cannot take to court.'
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא explains both halves of רבי חנינא's ruling using the case from step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First half: the land is still holy and the grain is still obligated, because a גוי's ownership cannot cancel the מעשר obligation. Second half: the buyer took over the גוי's rights. A כהן or לוי has no claim against a גוי, so they have no claim against the buyer either.

keyTerms.meaning: A גוי's ownership in ארץ ישראל does not remove its holiness
On the strength of, standing in the place of

steps.whatToRemember: Split ruling: the grain is obligated, so he must separate. But the buyer inherits the גוי's freedom from any claim by a כהן or לוי, so he keeps the portions.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a clear source for the idea that אין קנין לגוי בארץ ישראל להפקיע מיד מעשר. It also introduces the 'בא מכח' argument: a buyer can be in no worse position than the person he bought from.

phrases.english: He tithes them,
because a gentile has no acquisition [power] in Eretz Yisrael
to remove it from the obligation of tithes,
and they are his —
because he says to him: I come on the strength of a man
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the כהן or לוי who wants the portions. The 'man' is the non-Jew he bought from.

phrases.english: with whom you cannot engage in litigation.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Either way it means 'to have a court case'.

steps.triggerLanguage: מעשרן, דאין קנין לגוי בארץ ישראל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains both halves of רבי חנינא's ruling based on the case set up in step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The obligation exists because a גוי cannot cancel the land's holiness. The buyer keeps the portions because he comes 'מכח' the גוי, against whom the כהן has no claim.

steps.title: New source: produce deposited with a כותי or an עם הארץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from דמאי: produce left with a כותי or an עם הארץ keeps its original status regarding מעשר and שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: one who leaves his produce on deposit with a כותי or with an עם הארץ, it keeps its original status regarding מעשר and שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion by quoting a משנה from somewhere else. This sets up the analysis that will follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that we do not suspect the person holding the deposit of swapping the owner's produce for untithed produce or produce of שביעית. So the owner can treat it just as it was when he left it. The גמרא will now examine this ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
One who leaves something on deposit
A Jew not trusted about tithing

steps.confusionAlert: 'Keeps its status' means we do not suspect a swap. If the produce was already tithed, it stays tithed. It does not mean the holder made it tithed.

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מסכת דמאי.

phrases.english: One who deposits his produce with a Samaritan
or with an am ha'aretz,
they remain in their presumptive status regarding tithes and the Sabbatical Year.

steps.triggerLanguage: תנן התם: המפקיד פירותיו אצל הכותי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion after the previous line of reasoning ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Produce deposited with a כותי or an עם הארץ keeps its original status regarding מעשר and שביעית.

steps.title: Produce left with a gentile
steps.stepSummary: The משנה from דמאי continues: produce left with a גוי is treated like the גוי's own produce, while רבי שמעון says it is treated as דמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone left his produce with a gentile, it is treated like the gentile's produce. רבי שמעון says it is דמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה from דמאי that it started in the last step, now covering produce left with a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא assumes the גוי swapped the Jew's produce for his own, so what comes back is treated as the גוי's produce. רבי שמעון holds that we are only unsure whether a swap happened, so the produce gets the doubtful status of דמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce we are unsure was tithed

phrases.english: With a gentile, it is like his produce,
phrases.notes: "His" means the gentile's. The idea is that he probably swapped your produce for his own.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: it is demai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה quoted in step 6 by adding the case of a גוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Produce left with a גוי has the status of the גוי's produce according to the תנא קמא, and the status of דמאי according to רבי שמעון.

steps.title: What the dispute is really about
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that both sides agree the owner must separate the portions. They argue only about whether he must give them to a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Everyone agrees that he must separate the portions. They argue only about giving them to a כהן. The תנא קמא holds that the גוי definitely swapped the produce, so the owner must give the portions to a כהן. רבי שמעון holds that it is only דמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר narrows down the argument in the משנה and explains each side's thinking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Separating the portions is required either way, so that is not the argument. The תנא קמא is sure a swap happened, so the produce is definitely untithed and the כהן must receive his portion. רבי שמעון sees only a doubt, so the produce is treated as דמאי and the owner does not have to hand the portion over.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
About separating, everyone agrees,
phrases.notes: Both sides agree you must set aside the תרומה and מעשר from this produce.

phrases.english: where they disagree is about giving them to a priest.
The first tanna holds: he definitely swapped them,
phrases.notes: "He" is the גוי, who is assumed to have traded the Jew's produce for his own.

phrases.english: so he must give them to a priest,
and Rabbi Shimon holds: it is demai.
phrases.notes: Since it is only a doubt, the owner does not have to hand the portions to the כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לְהַפְרִישׁ כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the dispute in the משנה just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone requires separating the portions. The argument is only about whether they must be given to a כהן, and that depends on whether the swap is certain or doubtful.

steps.title: אביי challenges from the case of buying grain from a gentile
steps.stepSummary: אביי points out that, according to רבי אלעזר, a certain swap would require giving the portions to a כהן. That clashes with רבי חנינא's rule that someone who buys smoothed טבל from a גוי tithes it but keeps the portions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי sat and taught this teaching. אביי said to him: The only reason רבי שמעון disagrees is that we are unsure whether the גוי swapped the produce. So if he definitely swapped it, everyone would agree the portions must go to a כהן. But didn't רבי שמואל say in the name of רבי חנינא: Someone who buys smoothed טבל from a גוי tithes it, and the portions are his?
steps.whatsHappening: While רב דימי teaches רבי אלעזר's explanation, אביי raises a contradiction with an earlier ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From רבי אלעזר it follows that when the produce is definitely the גוי's, everyone requires giving the portions to a כהן. Yet רבי חנינא, discussed earlier in step 5, says that someone who acquires smoothed produce from a גוי keeps the portions himself. The two rulings seem to point in opposite directions.

keyTerms.meaning: And they are his (he keeps the portions)
But didn't (so-and-so) say?! A challenge formula

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב דִּימִי וְקָאָמַר לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא,
phrases.english: Rav Dimi sat and was saying this teaching,
phrases.notes: "This teaching" is רבי אלעזר's explanation from the step before.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
The reason is that we are unsure
whether he swapped them or did not swap them,
but if he definitely swapped them,
everyone agrees he must give them to a priest,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: but didn't Rabbi Shmuel say in the name of Rabbi Chanina:
One who buys untithed produce from a gentile, already smoothed,
phrases.notes: This is the same ruling the גמרא worked through earlier, back in steps 2 to 5.

phrases.english: tithes them, and they are his!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from רבי אלעזר's explanation and sets it against רבי חנינא's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim that everyone requires giving the portions to a כהן when the swap is certain.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי חנינא rules that produce acquired from a גוי is tithed but the portions stay with the owner. That contradicts the idea that certain גוי produce requires giving to a כהן.

steps.title: Two different kinds of תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The answer suggests that the requirement to give to a כהן refers to תרומה גדולה, while רבי חנינא's "they are his" refers to תרומת מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps here it is talking about תרומה גדולה, and there it is talking about תרומת מעשר!
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי answers אביי's challenge by saying the two rulings may be about different portions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's case, where the portion must go to the כהן, is about תרומה גדולה. רבי חנינא's case, where the owner keeps it, is about תרומת מעשר. Once each ruling refers to a different portion, they no longer contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: The main תרומה, separated first from the produce
The תרומה separated from the מעשר

steps.confusionAlert: The first "כאן" (here) is the משנה, where the portion goes to the כהן. The second "כאן" (there) is רבי חנינא's ruling, where he keeps it.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule "give it to the כהן" and the rule "it is his" can both stand, because they may refer to different portions: תרומה גדולה and תרומת מעשר.

phrases.english: Perhaps here it is about the great teruma,
phrases.notes: "Here" is the משנה, where the owner must give the portion to the כהן. This answers אביי's question.

phrases.english: and there it is about the teruma of the tithe!
phrases.notes: "There" is רבי חנינא's case, where the buyer keeps the portion.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא כָּאן בִּתְרוּמָה גְּדוֹלָה כָּאן בִּתְרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each ruling refers to a different type of תרומה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings seemed to be about the same portion, so they appeared to clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's requirement to give to a כהן is about תרומה גדולה, and רבי חנינא's "they are his" is about תרומת מעשר.

steps.title: אביי recalls a verse-based source for exemption from the tithe-gift
steps.stepSummary: אביי remembers that רבי יהושע בן לוי learned from a פסוק that טבל bought from a גוי does not require giving תרומת מעשר to a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: You reminded me of what רבי יהושע בן לוי said: How do we know that someone who buys smoothed טבל from a גוי is exempt from תרומת מעשר? The פסוק says, "Speak to the לוים... when you take from the children of Israel." From this we learn that with טבל you buy from Jews, you separate תרומת מעשר and give it to a כהן. With טבל you buy from a גוי, you do not separate it and give it to a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The last answer said that רבי חנינא's phrase "they are his" refers to תרומת מעשר. אביי now remembers a teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי that supports exactly this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the tithe-gift says "when you take from the children of Israel." רבי יהושע בן לוי reads this as limiting the duty to produce that came from Jews. So for produce bought from a גוי, there is no duty to give תרומת מעשר to a כהן. This fits the answer from step 10 that the buyer keeps the תרומת מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce from which the required portions have not yet been taken
Smoothed into a pile, the final step of processing that triggers the tithing obligation
The tenth of the לוי's tithe that is given to a כהן
From where do we know? (asking for a source)

steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a פסוק as the basis for the distinction made in step 10. That turns the answer from a guess into an established rule.

phrases.english: You reminded me of a matter
phrases.notes: אביי is the one speaking here. Something just said jogged his memory of an earlier teaching.

phrases.english: that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
From where do we know that one who buys smoothed untithed produce

phrases.aramaic: מִן הַגּוֹי שֶׁהוּא פָּטוּר מִתְּרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר?

As it is stated: "And to the Levites you shall speak,
phrases.notes: This פסוק is in במדבר פרק יח. It is where the תורה commands the לוים to give a tithe from their tithe.

phrases.english: and say to them: When you take
from the children of Israel"
untithed produce that you buy from Jews —

phrases.aramaic: אַתָּה מַפְרִישׁ מֵהֶן תְּרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר וְנוֹתְנָהּ לַכֹּהֵן,
phrases.english: you separate the teruma of the tithe from it and give it to the kohen,
untithed produce that you buy from a non-Jew —

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה מַפְרִישׁ מֵהֶן תְּרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר וְנוֹתְנָהּ לַכֹּהֵן.
phrases.english: you do not separate the teruma of the tithe from it and give it to the kohen.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַזְכַּרְתַּן מִילְּתָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that supports the answer in step 10, that "they are his" refers to תרומת מעשר
steps.raayaObject: That טבל bought from a גוי does not require giving תרומת מעשר to a כהן
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע בן לוי's reading of "כי תקחו מאת בני ישראל" (במדבר יח:כו)

steps.title: The משנה: if the redemption lamb dies, one may benefit from it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes its ruling that if the lamb used to redeem a פטר חמור dies, one may benefit from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: And if it dies, people may benefit from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the side topic and goes back to quoting the משנה about the redemption lamb. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The "it" here is the lamb given to redeem a firstborn donkey. The משנה rules that its carcass may be used for benefit and is not forbidden. The גמרא will next ask what new thing this teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: Derive benefit, make use of it

phrases.english: And if it dies, one may derive benefit from it.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה. "It" is the lamb used to redeem a firstborn donkey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the תרומת מעשר discussion and returns to the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A redemption lamb that died may be used for benefit

steps.title: Where did the lamb die? Either way the ruling seems obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the lamb died. In the כהן's house or in the owner's house, the ruling seems too obvious to need stating.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where did it die? If you say it died in the כהן's house and the כהן may benefit from it, that is obvious, since it is his property! Rather, say it died in the owner's house and the כהן may benefit from it. That too is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling as obvious. It tries two possible cases and finds nothing new in either one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the lamb died after the כהן received it, of course he may use what he owns. The second option is that it died before he received it, and the כהן still benefits. The גמרא calls this obvious too, since the lamb was already designated as his. So the challenge is: what is the משנה adding?

keyTerms.meaning: The owner (here, the Jew who owned the donkey)

phrases.english: Where did it die?
If you say that it died in the kohen's house,
and the kohen may benefit from it —
that is obvious, it is his own property!
Rather, say it died in the owner's house
and the kohen may benefit from it —
this too is obvious!

steps.title: The lamb belongs to the כהן from the moment it is separated
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is needed. Without it, we might have thought the כהן owns the lamb only once he receives it. The משנה teaches that he owns it from the moment it is separated.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought that as long as the lamb has not reached the כהן's hands, he has not acquired it. So the משנה teaches us that from the time the owner separated it, it stands in the כהן's possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the "obvious" challenge. It explains what we might have wrongly thought without the משנה's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this ruling, one could think the כהן acquires the lamb only when it is handed to him. Then a lamb that died in the owner's house would still be the owner's loss. The משנה teaches that the act of separating already puts the lamb in the כהן's ownership. So the כהן benefits from the carcass even if it died before he received it.
